scope: Corollary 1.3 (Smooth scalar uniqueness from one patch) of the manuscript “Smooth anisotropic uniqueness in the Calderón problem from one boundary patch” (preprints/Smooth-Anisotropic-Uniqueness-in-the-Calderon-Problem-from-One-Boundary-Patch-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 365 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1ec46ed64206d12d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let n ≥ 3, and let Ω and Γ be as above. If two strictly positive conductivities γ1, γ2 ∈ C∞(Ω) satisfy ΛΓ γ1 f = ΛΓ γ2 f for every f ∈ C∞ c (Γ), then γ1 = γ2 on Ω.
